Cloud Atlas by David Mitchell. It, as a novel, is rather hard to describe in any succinct fashion, but I'm just going to say that it's roughly one novel composed of 6 individual stories of wildly varying genre, tone and setting tied together by recurring imagery, characters and themes. The first story in the chronology starts in the early 19th century in the colonized South Pacific, and the last chronological story takes place in Hawaii hundreds of years after the collapse of modern civilization, to give you an idea of the sort of range we're looking at. Not to mention the fact that each story often varies wildly in format, with the first two being epistolary in nature, the middle two being in a fairly straightforward novelistic format, and the last two being formatted as oral retellings and interrogations around the events depicted within. Very readable and comprehensible, just don't expect to catch everything the first time.
